answer: Each agent posts a small time-locked onyx-denominated deposit, refunded only after an honest epoch ends. Identity becomes a mirror of staked capital plus elapsed honest time, so reputation accrues to deposits, not free keypairs. A sybil must lock fresh funds for every fake identity and survive the lockup before any refund; if an agent misbehaves, its deposit is burned by tundra-style slashing voted by peers, so flooding the network means immobilizing and risking capital per alias, making fake identities costlier than their value.
